name: Rotating the Array Values to the Right by One Position
description: Construct a program that has a method that receives an array of values and returns the array rotated to the right by one position so that the value that is currently at the end of the array is moved to the front, shifting the remaining values to the right. For example, if the array is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, the program will change it to {6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

comments.content: This statement declares the method rotateRight that takes an array, rotates the array to the right, and returns the rotated array.

The value at the end of the array is supposed to go to the front of the array, and the other values are supposed to rotate backward. We can make the task easier by storing the value at the end of the array into a local variable and then shift the other values to the right by one position.

This statement stores the value of the element at the end of the array that is located at index lst.length-1 to the variable last.
The expression lst.length returns the number of the values in the array. We will use variable last later to move the value at the end to the front of the array.

With value at the end safely tucked away, we now have to shift the remaining values to the right by one position. We could break down the overall task into shifting operations, each of which is a simple assignment statement. Because of repeated shift operations on the array elements, we’d want to write this with a for loop. We’ll replace element at index i with the value currently stored in the element at index i-1, this will shift value at index i-1 to the right, by one position. We'll put this line of code inside the for loop.

To properly shift the elements to the right, we have to run the loop in reverse order (from right to left instead of left to right).

Note that we need to terminate the loop when the control variable reaches 0 because in the assignment statement in the loop body we always move the element one position before the element at the current index. That is, when we get into index 1, we move the element at index 0 to index 1.

Also note that the decrement operator (--) subtract 1 from the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i - 1.
We need to shift value at index i-1 to value at index i. We do this by setting the value at index i to the value at index i-1.

After shifting the values to the right, we’ve made room at the front of the array for the value that used to be at the end of the array (which is currently stored in a local variable called last). This statement copies the value of variable last to the first element of the array.
Note that 0 is the index of the first element in the array.
Now that we finished rotating the array elements, we need to return the rotated array. The return statement, when reached, ends the method call and sends the result back to the caller.
We define this method to print the elements in an int array.

To print the array elements, we need to traverse the array and then print each element as we visit it. We traverse the array elements using for–each statement. This for loop assigns the name x to each of the elements in the array in turn, from left to right, and the print statement will be executed for each.
This statement prints the element that we visited in the array followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements of the array in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.
This statement adds an end-of-line (new line) character to the end of the array elements.
We define array referred by variable values to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.
This statement prints the elements of the array by calling the print method.

This statement first calls the rotateRight method and passes the array as its argument. After that, it prints the returned array from the method call by calling the print method. The printed array is the rotated array.

Note that any changes that were made to the array within the rotateRight method affect the original array in the calling method. That is, after the method call, the array referred by variables values will be changed to the rotated array.
